title: Assignment 04 · Consideration and interpretation
summary: Consideration and interpretation. Assigned readings and principal cases for this class.
notes:
Mattei v. Hopper: A purchaser’s satisfaction condition did not make his promise illusory because he had to exercise his judgment about the proposed leases in good faith.

Structural Polymer Group, Ltd. v. Zoltek Corp.: A requirements contract remained enforceable despite uncertain quantity and purchasing flexibility because exclusivity, a matching right, and good faith constrained the buyer’s choices.

Wood v. Lucy, Lady Duff-Gordon: The exclusive agency agreement carried an implied promise to use reasonable efforts, drawn from its structure and compensation terms, so it was not unenforceable for want of an undertaking by Wood.

Additional assigned materials: UCC § 2-306; Agreement in Wood (SEL).
